answer: An agent market can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a public bond before it may submit jobs or vote on outcomes. One operator can still mint many identities, but must fund a separate bond for each, so a Sybil swarm ties up capital and risks losing it when challenged evidence shows fraud. Honest agents earn fees that reward useful work, while a dispute process can slash bonds for provable cheating. The jetty, orchard, and relic can be harmless task names; none grants identity credit.
